S1.rationale: AgentRuntime composes an ordinary tool-observing ReAct agent with caller-provided inference and bounded session/checkpoint handling. No particular tool-loop defect or affected user behavior was substantiated in the native issue check.

S2.rationale: The negotiation module accepts competing agent compute/memory/token proposals and applies deterministic allocation strategies to return resource outcomes. This is already an inter-S1 resource conflict attenuation, although downstream integration owns actual enforcement; no specific broken allocation case is reported.

S3.rationale: AgentSupervisor and Erlang-style supervised child restarts apply one-for-one/group policies and escalation under current failure-state observation. These are real deterministic S3 mechanisms, not proof that adding discretionary model management would improve reliability.

S3*.rationale: A separate shadow traffic path pairs sampled production and shadow responses and reports divergences for possible follow-up. It supports S3* comparison under configured assumptions; no concrete false-divergence or missing remediation requirement was established by the bounded assessment.

S4.rationale: Temporal belief history, reflection, memory consolidation and planning can change local context but do not establish an outside-and-then organizational capability adaptation decision. No native demand for an external-prospective loop was observed.

S5.rationale: PolicyStore RBAC conditions, roles, allow/deny limits and runtime config enforce already-authored choices rather than resolve ultimate purpose/identity disputes. No supported S5 redesign candidate is implied by the absent function.
